_about: Common benign network patterns. A match is shown as 'probably X' and lowers the alert's severity; it never hides an alert. Commands are templates shown to the user to copy; Vigil never runs them. {pkg_install}, {pkg_remove} and {pkg_owner} are filled in for the detected distro; {pkg} is the package name for that distro.

services.name: NetworkManager's connectivity check
services.what: NetworkManager fetches a tiny text file over plain HTTP every 5 minutes to check that the internet really works. Arch uses ping.archlinux.org; other distros use their own address.
services.why_fine: It is how your desktop detects hotel and airport login pages, and shows 'limited connectivity'. It sends nothing about you.
services.privacy: The check is unencrypted, so your network can see that this PC runs NetworkManager on your distro. The distro's server sees your IP address every 5 minutes.

check.title: Show NetworkManager's connectivity settings
check.what: Prints the configuration NetworkManager is using, including the check address and interval.

check.title: Ask NetworkManager what it currently thinks
check.what: Shows full, limited, portal or none.

fix.title: Turn off NetworkManager's connectivity check
fix.what: Adds a small config file that disables the check, then reloads NetworkManager.
fix.lose: Login pages for hotel or airport Wi-Fi no longer pop up by themselves, and the 'limited connectivity' warning disappears.

services.name: Syncthing discovery and relays
services.what: Syncthing announces your device to its global discovery servers and keeps contact with relay servers, so your other devices can find it. It also checks for upgrades and may send anonymous usage reports.
services.why_fine: This is how Syncthing connects your devices across networks. The relay and discovery servers are run by volunteers, often on Hetzner or similar hosts.
services.privacy: Discovery servers learn your device ID and IP address. File contents are always encrypted between devices; relays cannot read them.

check.title: Is Syncthing running as your user service?
check.what: Shows whether the Syncthing user service is active and since when.

fix.title: Stop Syncthing talking to public servers
fix.what: Turns off global discovery, relaying, usage reports and automatic upgrades. Devices on the same network still find each other.
fix.lose: Devices on other networks can no longer reach this one unless you enter their addresses by hand.
steps: Open the Syncthing web interface: http://127.0.0.1:8384
Actions → Settings → Connections: untick 'Global Discovery' and 'Enable Relaying'
Settings → General: set 'Anonymous Usage Reporting' to Disabled and 'Automatic upgrades' to Off
undo_steps: Connections: tick 'Global Discovery' and 'Enable Relaying' again

fix.title: Stop Syncthing and keep it from starting
fix.what: Stops the Syncthing user service now and at every login.

fix.title: Uninstall Syncthing
fix.what: Removes the Syncthing package. Your synced files stay where they are.

services.name: Browser background requests (Firefox family)
services.what: Besides the pages you open, the browser checks for updates, downloads its block lists and settings, keeps a push-notification connection and, in Firefox, checks for captive portals over plain HTTP.
services.why_fine: These are the browser maintaining itself. LibreWolf turns most of them off already; the ones left are mostly updates and block lists.
services.privacy: Mozilla's servers see your IP address and browser version. Safe Browsing checks send partial hashes of addresses, not the addresses themselves.

check.title: See what the browser is connected to
check.what: Open about:networking in the browser; the Sockets and DNS tabs list every active connection and the names behind them.
steps: In the browser's address bar, open about:networking
Look at 'Sockets' (open connections) and 'DNS' (names it resolved)

fix.title: Turn off captive-portal checks (plain HTTP)
fix.what: Stops the browser fetching detectportal.firefox.com over HTTP whenever the network changes.
fix.lose: Hotel and airport login pages are no longer detected by the browser.
steps: Open about:config and accept the warning
Search for network.captive-portal-service.enabled and set it to false
Search for network.connectivity-service.enabled and set it to false

fix.title: Turn off web push notifications
fix.what: Closes the long-lived connection to Mozilla's push service.
fix.lose: Sites can no longer send you notifications while closed.

fix.title: Turn off Safe Browsing lookups
fix.what: Stops downloading Google's Safe Browsing lists.
fix.lose: No more warnings for known phishing and malware sites. Not recommended.
undo_steps: Tick 'Block dangerous and deceptive content' again

services.name: Browser background requests (Chromium family)
services.what: Chromium-based browsers check for updates and extension updates, fetch Safe Browsing lists and keep a push connection (port 5228) open.
services.why_fine: These keep the browser and its extensions current and power site notifications.
services.privacy: Google (or the browser vendor) sees your IP address, browser version and extension IDs during update checks.

check.title: See what the browser is connected to
check.what: chrome://net-internals and chrome://net-export show the browser's own connections.
steps: Or open chrome://net-export to record a short capture

fix.title: Turn off background apps
fix.what: Stops the browser running in the background after you close it.
fix.lose: Extensions and apps that work while the browser is closed stop doing so.
steps: Turn off 'Continue running background apps when the browser is closed'
undo_steps: Turn 'Continue running background apps when the browser is closed' back on

fix.title: Turn off Safe Browsing
fix.what: Stops Safe Browsing list downloads and lookups.
fix.lose: No more warnings for known dangerous sites. Not recommended.

services.name: Network time sync (NTP)
services.what: Your clock is kept accurate by asking time servers every few minutes.
services.why_fine: Accurate time matters: certificates and logins fail when the clock is wrong.
services.privacy: Plain NTP is unauthenticated: the time servers see your IP. NTS (port 4460) adds authentication.

check.title: Show time sync status
check.what: Which server is used, and how far off the clock is.

check.title: Show chrony's sources (if chrony is installed)
check.what: Lists the time servers chrony uses.

fix.title: Turn off automatic time sync
fix.what: Stops the system asking time servers.
fix.lose: Your clock drifts; after a while secure websites and logins start failing. Not recommended.

services.name: Package manager mirror sync
services.what: Your package manager (or a timer such as dnf-makecache or apt-daily) refreshes its list of available updates from a mirror.
services.why_fine: This is how updates arrive. Mirrors are run by universities and hosting companies, so their owners vary.
services.privacy: The mirror sees your IP address and which packages you download. Plain HTTP mirrors are signed but readable by your network.

check.title: List the timers that refresh packages
check.what: Shows when each scheduled job last ran and runs next.

fix.title: Stop automatic package list refreshes
fix.lose: Update notifications appear later; updating still works.

fix.title: Stop automatic package list refreshes
fix.lose: Update notifications appear later; updating still works.

fix.title: Stop reflector's mirror refreshes
fix.what: Disables the reflector timer, if you use it.
fix.lose: Your mirror list stops updating itself.

services.name: Desktop update checks (Flatpak, Discover, GNOME Software, PackageKit)
services.what: Your desktop's software centre checks for app, Flatpak and firmware updates in the background.
services.why_fine: It keeps apps and firmware patched and shows update notifications.
services.privacy: Flathub and the firmware service see your IP address and which apps or devices are checked.

check.title: Is PackageKit running?
check.what: Shows whether the PackageKit service is active.

check.title: List installed Flatpak remotes
check.what: Shows which Flatpak repositories are checked for updates.

fix.title: Stop GNOME Software downloading updates in the background
fix.what: GNOME Software stops automatic update downloads.
fix.lose: You update by hand from GNOME Software.

fix.title: Turn off Discover's update notifications
fix.what: KDE Discover stops checking for updates in the background.
fix.lose: No update notifications; update from Discover by hand.
undo_steps: Set 'Notification frequency' back to Daily or Weekly

fix.title: Stop PackageKit from starting
fix.what: Masks the PackageKit service so software centres cannot start it.
fix.lose: Software centres can no longer install or update packages.
